name: The Kilianseiche of Schesslitz

location.address: Junction of Hauptstrasse and the road to the cemetery, near the Ziegelmuehle, Schesslitz

verified_sources: https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liste_der_Naturdenkm%C3%A4ler_im_Landkreis_Bamberg (reproduces the Landkreis Bamberg ordinance of 2009: no. 61, ND-03526, 'Kilianseiche', Scheßlitz, Flurstueck 94/2, coordinates 49.97709, 11.03641)
https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Category:Kilianseiche_(Scheßlitz) (photographs of the tree; Commons file 'Kilianseiche - panoramio.jpg' geotagged 16 m from the register point)
access: Free. Stands at a road junction on the way to the village cemetery, on public ground as far as the register wording shows ('an der Abzweigung der Hauptstrasse zum Friedhof'); not checked against OSM tags.
transport: About 15 km north of Bamberg. Regional bus from Bamberg ZOB to the Schesslitz Kilianskirche stop, roughly 25 minutes (line 969 in the 2024 VGN timetable; check the current one), then on foot to the junction of the Hauptstrasse and the road to the cemetery.
verify_notes: Register only, one source (Bavarian LfU point layer ND-03526 plus the Landkreis ordinance reproduced on de.wikipedia). The register gives NO species, girth, height or age: 'Kilianseiche' means 'Kilian's oak' so oak is inferred from the name only, not from a record; call it an oak and leave the species a question for readers. Alive: weak. lifecheck returned RECENT 2025-01-06 but that match was a beer-glass photograph 16 m away, not the tree, so it proves nothing; the only tree image is an old Panoramio upload on Commons. Page should say the register lists it and ask readers to confirm it stands. Pin is the register's tree-level point and a geotagged Commons photograph sits 16 m from it, so confirmed is defensible but not checked against aerial imagery. Photograph in reach (Commons category). Why it is worth a stop: it is one of the few named (not just numbered) monuments in the district, named for Saint Kilian, the patron of Schesslitz's parish church (the church's St. Kilian dedication is visible in nearby Commons file names; no tree history sourced, writer must not invent one). Same ordinance also lists no. 62 'Eiche' at the Demmelsdorfer Strasse / Altenbach junction (49.97416, 11.03862, Flurstueck 536), about 300 m away, a plain unnamed oak, not delivered.
story:
Most protected trees in the Bamberg district get a number. This one got a name. The district's 2009 ordinance lists natural monument 61 as the Kilianseiche, Kilian's oak, standing where the Hauptstrasse in Schesslitz turns off toward the cemetery. A plain oak a few hundred metres away, number 62, is listed simply as an oak.

The name is nearly all the register gives. It records no species, no girth, no height and no age, so even calling this an oak rests on the name rather than on a survey. Which oak it is, and how old, are questions this page cannot answer yet.

The name does point somewhere. The parish church in Schesslitz is dedicated to Saint Kilian, and the bus from Bamberg stops at a halt called Kilianskirche. Whether the tree was named for the church, or for some older reason, no source we have found says, so we will not invent a story for it.

Then the caveat that matters most. The only photograph of the tree we can find is an old upload to the Panoramio photo site, taken sixteen metres from the register's point, and there is nothing recent. The ordinance still protects it, but we cannot show you dated proof that it stands.

Schesslitz is about fifteen kilometres north of Bamberg, roughly twenty-five minutes on the regional bus. If you make the trip, tell us whether Kilian's oak is still at its junction, and if you know your oaks, which kind it is.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by where it stands: at the junction where the Hauptstrasse in Schesslitz turns off toward the cemetery, near the Ziegelmuehle. An unnamed protected oak stands 300 metres away on the Demmelsdorfer Strasse.

name: The Maple of Dörfleins

location.address: Field north of Dörfleins, Fl.Nr. 4050, Gemarkung Hallstadt

verified_sources: https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liste_der_Naturdenkm%C3%A4ler_im_Landkreis_Bamberg (reproduces Landkreis Bamberg register: ND-06940, 'Ahorn nördlich von Dörfleins', Fl.Nr. 4050, schutzgrund quoted)

https://www.landkreis-bamberg.de/loadDocument.phtml?ObjSvrID=1633&ObjID=4084&ObjLa=1&Ext=PDF (Verordnung über das Naturdenkmal Ahorn nördlich von Dörfleins, 30 April 2010; fetched and read: protects the maple on Fl.Nr. 4050, 10 m surrounding zone)
https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Category:Ahorn_n%C3%B6rdlich_von_D%C3%B6rfleins (ten geotagged photographs by Stephan van Helden, 17 Feb 2024, CC BY-SA 4.0)

official_register.name: Bayerisches Landesamt für Umwelt Naturdenkmal ND-06940 / Landkreis Bamberg ordinance 2010

access: Not stated by a source. Stands on a field parcel north of the village; no access tags checked (Overpass unreachable). Viewable from the field edge as far as the 2024 photographs show; unverified whether a footpath reaches it.
transport: Dörfleins is part of Hallstadt, about 7 km north of Bamberg centre. Bus timetable not checked.
verify_notes: Register plus ordinance (one official source, owner of the ground's regulator) plus 10 Commons photographs dated Feb 2024, so alive as of 2024-02-17. Register point 49.93652,10.86397; photographer GPS fixes cluster at 49.93637-49.93642, 10.86374-10.86391, within about 15 m of it, so the pin is confirmed by GPS at the tree. Ordinance names only 'Ahorn' (genus Acer), no girth, height or age; species left as a question for readers. Official protection reason, quoted from the Wikipedia list's Schutzgrund column: the tree 'bereichert und prägt durch seine Schönheit und Dominanz das Ortsbild' (enriches and shapes the village scene by its beauty and dominance). Ordinance sets a 10 m protected zone around it. Photograph in reach: Commons category above (Stephan van Helden, CC BY-SA 4.0, user Plozessor). Another register oak (ND-04404, Kilianstraße cul-de-sac, already a lead) stands about 700 m away in the same village, but is not a delivered tree. Not a spectacular-age claim: do not call it old. The register has no vitality field; 2024 photographs are the life evidence.
story:
In April 2010 the district of Bamberg passed a law about one maple. The ordinance is titled for the Ahorn nördlich von Dörfleins, the maple north of Dörfleins, and it covers a single tree on a single field parcel, number 4050, with a protected zone ten metres around it.

The reason it gives is not age. In the official wording, the tree enriches and shapes the look of the village through its beauty and its dominance. That is a planning office saying, as plainly as planning offices ever do, that this is the tree people in Dörfleins see when they look north across the fields.

The paperwork stops there. It records no species beyond maple, no girth, no height and no planting date, so we will not call it old and we will not guess at a number. What we can show is that it stands: a photographer recorded it for Wikimedia Commons on 17 February 2024, ten pictures taken within about fifteen metres of the trunk.

Dörfleins is part of Hallstadt, about seven kilometres north of Bamberg's centre. A protected oak stands about 700 metres away in the same village. No source we found says whether a footpath reaches the maple itself; the 2024 photographs were taken from the field edge, and that is where to stand.

Sycamore, Norway maple or field maple: the register does not say which, and nobody has dated it. If you know either answer, tell us.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it as the maple standing in the field north of Dörfleins, on parcel 4050, inside a protected zone of ten metres. The village's other protected tree, an oak, is about 700 metres away.

access: Not stated by a source. The register places it in a 'Baumfeld' (tree field) beside a consolidation farm track; presumably reachable on foot along that track but not verified (OSM tags unreachable).
transport: Unterhaid is in Oberhaid, about 12 km west of Bamberg centre. Public transport not checked.

Register point and the photographs' GPS agree within about 6 m, so pin confirmed by GPS at the tree. No species beyond 'Linde' in the register; no girth, height or age found. story:
The official description of this tree runs to two words: 1 Linde, one lime. Bavaria's register of natural monuments lists it as ND-03903, the Bamberg district's list as number 48, on land parcel 669 at Unterhaid.

Where the record gets specific is the address. The lime stands about 200 metres north of the railway underpass, in what the register calls a Baumfeld, a tree field, on the east side of a farm track laid out when the fields here were consolidated. It is a precise way to find a tree and a thin way to describe one.

Everything a visitor usually asks about is missing. No species beyond lime, no girth, no height, no age. On Wikimedia Commons its photographs sit in a category called the big lime of Unterhaid, but that is somebody's label rather than a measurement, and we will not repeat it as one.

What those photographs do settle is that the tree was alive on 18 March 2023, and that the camera stood within about six metres of the register's point, so the pin is good.

Unterhaid belongs to Oberhaid, about twelve kilometres west of Bamberg's centre. The farm track beside the tree field is the likely way in, though no source we found confirms it, so treat this as a stop on a country walk rather than a destination in itself.

Nobody has dated this lime or named its species. If you have stood under it, tell us what you found.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by where it stands: in the tree field on the east side of the farm track, about 200 metres north of the railway underpass at Unterhaid.

story:
Bavaria's register gives directions to this lime the way a farmer would: on the high ground between Pödeldorf and Naisa, about 50 metres east of the edge of the village. It is natural monument ND-03734, number 46 on the Bamberg district's list, on land parcel 105.

That sentence of directions is most of what the register says. It names the tree only as a lime, with no species, no girth, no height and no age, and no source we found tells its history. What it has is a place: open ground, just where the village stops and the fields toward Naisa begin.

The proof of life is recent enough to trust. Two photographs on Wikimedia Commons, taken on 11 September 2023 and titled with its register number, show it standing. The camera that took them stood about 36 metres south-west of the register's point, though, which means neither the photographs nor the register fix the exact trunk, and our pin is marked approximate for that reason.

Pödeldorf is about four kilometres east of Bamberg's centre, close enough to make this a short outing from the city. No source confirms a path to the tree, so expect to view it from the field edge.

Nobody has published an age or the species of this lime. If you walk up to it and know which lime it is, or have a tape measure in your pocket, tell us.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it as the lime on the rise between Pödeldorf and Naisa, about 50 metres east of where the houses of Pödeldorf end.
